newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto party accuses Pakistan army of vote fraud.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto party accuses Pakistan army of vote fraud.

text.p: Former prime minister Benazir Bhuttos Pakistan Peoples Party dragged the army into allegations of vote rigging on Thursday.

PPP candidates, who suffered a crushing defeat in a general election on February 3, made the charge for the first time in speeches at a meeting with Bhutto in Lahore, capital of populous Punjab province.
Bhutto has already accused President Farooq Leghari and a caretaker government of rigging a landslide victory for the Pakistan Muslim League of her rival, former prime minister Nawaz Sharif.
But she says the army was not involved in Legharis sacking of her three-year-old government on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.

She did not her self attack the army in a brief speech to the Lahore meeting but said the PPP would not launch a protest agitation "because it would provide an opportunity to the armed forces to impose martial law".
About 250,000 army troops helped the civilian administration maintain peace across the country during polling on February 3.

"Almost without exception, the PPP candidates... complained of pre-poll and polling day rigging and irregularities," the official APP news agency reported. They also said voter turnout was lower than the official count of 35.92 percent of 53.88 million voters.

"The second consistent allegation they made was the presence of army personnel and their influence in coaxing voters to stamp ballot papers beside the...(Muslim League's tiger) symbol," the agency said.
The speakers accused troops of virtually controlling polling stations, stamping ballot papers and taking civilian officers who presided over voting into custody.
"Army conducted the elections while the Election Commission only supervised the action of the army," said a defeated PPP candidate from northern Punjab, Raja Munawar Ahmad.

Hamid Nasir Chatha, president of a breakaway Muslim League faction allied with the PPP, said army personnel played a major role in his defeat from an eastern Punjab constituency, keeping his supporters away from the polling stations while staff on duty stamped ballot papers in favour of his rival.

"Under a planned conspiracy, efforts were made to keep the Pakistan Peoples Party out of national politics," said Yousaf Raza Gillani, speaker of the former National Assembly who was defeated in southern Punjab.
Bhutto is due to hold a party meeting on Saturday to decide whether to sit in the new National Assembly or boycott it.
